Description: Unplanned failure of mixers, filling machines, wrapping units, or labeling systems.
Planned maintenance windows for cleaning, lubrication, calibration, or replacement of parts.
Extended setup or retooling time when switching between products or packaging formats.
Delayed or missing supply of raw materials such as detergents, resins, or fragrances.
Defective bottles, caps, pouches, or labels causing jams or stoppages on packaging lines.
Production halted while QA verifies product samples or addresses off-spec batches.
Mandatory cleaning or sanitation cycles between product runs or shifts.
Power fluctuation or loss of compressed air, chilled water, or steam required for production.
PLC or SCADA system fault, printer malfunction, or automation software error.
Incorrect setup parameters or SOP deviation by operator leading to line stoppage.
Safety incident, E-stop activation, or lockout/tagout procedures halting production.
Delays caused by poor communication or coordination between planning, maintenance, and operations.
Uncategorized or rare causes not captured under standard downtime factors.
